mechanics: A client command controls a default-enabled flag. A cancellable HEAD injection skips Lightmap.render while the flag is enabled.
The command text acknowledges that re-enabling the feature can require a restart. This is unconditional removal of the lightmap render path, not input-aware reuse of an equivalent result.
risks: Changes lighting appearance and can leave stale lightmap state. Cancelling a render/upload path does not prove all associated CPU calculations are avoided.
validation: Check day/night, dimension changes, darkness/night vision, toggling, and the actual lightmap producer/consumer paths.
disable-lighting.fit: Fullbright/lighting removal; incompatible with unchanged vanilla visuals.

mechanics: Wraps Display.updateCulling. Displays with nonzero width and height retain vanilla behavior; otherwise disables noCulling and constructs a world AABB.
Transforms eight corners of a padded generic model cube through the display transformation, accumulates componentwise minimum/maximum, and translates the bounds to entity position.
An invoker exposes the display's transformation construction.
risks: Generic padded cube bounds may not enclose arbitrarily long text, custom item/block models, or interpolated transforms. Conservative bounds must cover the rendered geometry at the actual partial tick.
Min/max start at the origin, which can enlarge bounds for wholly translated geometry. Extra inclusion is safe for visibility but reduces rejection efficiency.
validation: Test text displays with long lines, nonuniform scaling, rotations, interpolation, negative scales, large custom models, and screen-edge movement.
cull-display-entities.fit: Potentially useful display culling, but unchanged visuals require geometry-aware conservative bounds.

disable-portal-checks.scope: All four reconstructed classes reviewed; two contain initialization/empty example hooks.
mechanics: Intercepts the portal-placement open-position search and immediately returns its supplied fallback position.
Skips searching for a suitable open destination rather than accelerating an equivalent search. Some reconstructed Minecraft class names remain intermediary names.
risks: Can change destination placement and collision/suffocation outcomes around portals. Exact class/method mapping must be verified for the artifact's game version.
validation: Compare exits into obstructed areas, oversized entities, portals at borders, and destination collision outcomes.
disable-portal-checks.fit: Removes a gameplay correctness check; not a behavior-preserving optimization.

mechanics: Cancels most Entity.push(Entity) calls. The player-related branch preserves selected interactions but cancels when the incoming entity is a Mob; non-player interactions are cancelled.
Cancels Player.touch except for experience-orb and item entities. A separate empty collision mixin contributes no operation.
risks: Changes collision and touch behavior, including crowd mechanics. The player branch is asymmetric and requires both call directions to be checked.
validation: Check player/mob/player pairs in both directions, boats/minecarts, crowd pushing, pickups, and any touch-based entity behavior.
mob-collision-off.fit: Simulation work reduction through changed gameplay; excluded from unchanged-behavior optimization.

block-entity-rd.scope: All five reconstructed classes and config defaults reviewed.
mechanics: Stores squared render distances by block-entity type, with a default of 64 blocks for unspecified types and shorter configured defaults for many vanilla types.
In per-type mode, replaces shouldRender with squared camera-to-block-center distance comparison. In global mode, replaces the renderer view-distance getter using the global squared value.
Commands update enabled/global/distance settings and read/write a JSON config. Registry IDs map configured names to live block-entity types.
risks: Defaults hide visible block entities earlier than vanilla. Replacing shouldRender can bypass specialized renderer rules, not just change a threshold.
Reloaded config adds entries without a shown map clear, so removed entries can remain in memory. Parse failures can overwrite the existing file with current settings.
validation: Compare per-type visibility, specialized renderers and beams, invalid/removed config entries, mode switching, and resource/world changes.
block-entity-rd.fit: Distance cutbacks; incompatible with the requested 16–20 chunk scene and unchanged visuals.

fastorbs.scope: Both reconstructed classes reviewed; upstream repository identity checked.
mechanics: Replaces XP award creation with a nearby alive-orb lookup, adds one getExperienceValue(amount) result to an existing orb or spawns one orb, and resets its age.
Merging accepts any other alive orb, sums values, keeps the younger age, and discards the merged orb. Merge scans run on even server ticks in a slightly expanded bounding box.
Changes the pickup-delay constant from two ticks to zero.
risks: The award replacement shows one denomination selection and no loop consuming the remainder of amount. Total XP conservation must be checked against the selected vanilla implementation.
Merging any alive orb, age resets, enlarged scan region, and zero delay change orb distribution and collection behavior. Summed integer values can overflow at extreme amounts.
validation: For many award amounts, assert total spawned/merged XP equals the award. Check mending allocation, pickup cooldown, despawn, direction, large awards, and repeated merging.
fastorbs.fit: Fewer XP entities can save simulation/render work, but this implementation needs conservation and gameplay checks; do not transplant blindly.

mechanics: After persistent entity-section visibility changes, checks whether the entity is a moving WitherSkull on a ServerLevel.
If its position is no longer entity-ticking and velocity is nonzero, discards the skull instead of allowing it to persist through inactive chunks.
risks: Changes projectile lifetime and future effects after chunk reactivation. Non-ticking is not identical to permanently irrelevant.
validation: Track moving/stationary skulls through chunk unload/reload, ticking boundaries, forced chunks, and world save/restart.
non-persistent-wither-skulls.fit: Prevents accumulating projectiles by removing them; a server behavior change, not exact optimization.

fastchest-update.scope: All eight reconstructed Java classes reviewed; resource model appearance still requires resource/visual review.
mechanics: For enabled chest categories, returns null from block-entity render-state extraction, suppressing the dynamic chest renderer.
Mixin methods provide a block render shape via the superclass so static block models can render instead. Disabled categories return INVISIBLE so their dynamic renderer remains the intended path.
Configuration exposes normal, trapped, ender, and copper chest switches. Closing the config screen triggers a full level render rebuild.
risks: Static models replace animated geometry, including opening lids, so image/animation behavior changes. Resource models and texture variants determine the substitute appearance.
Per-category toggles must pair block-model and dynamic-renderer paths correctly or chests can disappear/double-render. High-priority render-shape overrides can overlap other mods.
validation: Check opening/closing, double chests, copper variants, seasonal textures, category toggles, resource reload, and chunk rebuilds.
fastchest-update.fit: Reduces dynamic-rendering work through static visual replacement; excluded from unchanged visuals.

rhenium-mod.scope: All nine reconstructed Java classes reviewed.
mechanics: Applies configured distance cutoffs to chest render eligibility, entity rendering, and particle ticking.
Cancels stationary grounded item ticks on three of four invocations. Cancels hopper pushItemsTick on eleven of twelve invocations while its cooldown is positive.
Config fields also advertise entity tick culling and chunk-load spreading, but no implementing hook for those fields is shown in these reconstructed classes.
risks: Skipping particle tick can freeze movement/age and delay expiry instead of merely avoiding invisible drawing. Skipping entire item ticks can alter despawn/pickup/timers.
Hopper cancellation may stop normal cooldown progression inside the cancelled method; transfer timing must be checked rather than assuming idle behavior is unchanged.

The entity-distance hook uses incoming coordinates as a world point; verify whether that call passes camera-relative coordinates. Config parsing catches I/O failures but not every malformed JSON/runtime failure.
validation: Inspect coordinate conventions and cooldown ownership. Test pickup/despawn, hopper throughput/cooldowns, distant particles returning to view, world switches, and malformed config.
rhenium-mod.fit: Mostly distance cuts and tick throttling with behavior changes; does not meet unchanged-visuals/behavior requirements as observed.

mechanics: A key binding toggles a client flag and overlay message. The EntityRenderer.shouldRender hook returns false for Player entities whose UUID differs from the local player's UUID while enabled.
No spatial occlusion test is involved; other players are hidden regardless of whether visible.
risks: Visible players disappear. Using render eligibility may affect attached labels/effects depending on the calling renderer.
validation: Check local third-person rendering, other players, spectator/camera states, labels, toggling, and reconnect.
player-hider-funnest-edition.fit: Visibility removal; excluded from unchanged visuals.

mechanics: Unconditionally cancels MapRenderer.render at method entry. The initializer has no additional behavior.
risks: Map image content is deliberately removed from rendering; this affects held/frame maps using this path.
validation: Check held maps, item-frame maps, decorations, labels, and other map render integrations.
map-rendering-disabler.fit: Content suppression utility, not unchanged-visuals optimization.

mechanics: At play-connection initialization, saves the current render distance and lowers it to two chunks when enabled for that connection type.
After join, waits 100 client ticks, then restores two chunks every 20 ticks until the original distance is reached. Disconnect restores immediately and resets state.
Singleplayer and multiplayer switches are persisted in JSON and exposed through a config screen.
risks: Temporarily changes visible distance and chunk request/render workload. A user changing render distance during restoration can have their change overwritten by the saved original.
validation: Test interrupted joins, quick reconnects, dimension changes, edits during restoration, options availability, and malformed config.
smooth-join.fit: Spreads join work by a temporary distance reduction; excluded from the unchanged-distance requirement.

mechanics: When serializing an Identifier in the default minecraft namespace, writes only its path instead of the namespace-prefixed string.

Replaces the Identifier stream codec with UTF-8 mapping whose decoder uses Identifier.parse and whose encoder applies the same default-namespace shortening. Non-default namespaces keep their complete strings.
risks: Requires receiver parsing to assign the omitted namespace identically. External protocol consumers may expect an explicitly qualified string.
Savings depend on how many identifiers are sent; parsing and allocations remain. Compatibility includes wire semantics, not only local round trips.
validation: Round-trip default/custom namespaces and malformed IDs through both encoding paths, connect to ordinary clients/servers, and measure actual encoded bytes.
resource-trimmer.fit: Small network payload reduction; not a general rendering FPS improvement.

recipecooldown.scope: All four top-level reconstructed classes reviewed; embedded config library not reviewed.
mechanics: At server recipe-placement packet entry, compares wall-clock time to the last accepted craft request by player UUID. Cancels requests within the configured cooldown, default 50 milliseconds.
A tail hook records the current time after accepted requests. Configuration supports enable/disable and migrates a legacy first-line delay file to the current format.
risks: Rate limiting drops gameplay requests rather than processing them faster. Wall-clock adjustments can affect cooldown comparisons.
No logout cleanup of the UUID-to-time map is shown. Long-running servers with many distinct players can retain entries.
validation: Test boundary timing, rapid requests, disabled mode, reconnects, wall-clock changes, malformed legacy config, and long-run map size.
recipecooldown.fit: Server request-rate protection, not behavior-preserving FPS optimization.
